label: Время
description: The heteroclitic neuter noun время ("time"). Oblique singular forms insert the -ен- stem (времени, временем), a hallmark of the -мя declension class.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 1. 'Время' is the neuter subject in its base nominative form (no -ен- stem). 2. 'Идёт' agrees as a 3rd-person singular verb. 3. The sentence means time goes by very fast.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 1. 'Нет' forces the genitive. 2. 'Времени' uses the heteroclitic -ен- oblique stem, not 'врема'. 3. The core phrase means I have no time at all.
Strategic focus: Genitive after quantity. 1. 'Много' governs the genitive. 2. 'Времени' shows the -ен- oblique stem of this -мя noun. 3. The sentence means this will take a lot of time.
Strategic focus: Genitive question. 1. 'Сколько' takes the genitive. 2. 'Времени' again inserts the heteroclitic -ен- oblique stem. 3. The question asks what time it is now.

missions.phrase: К этому времени все уже ушли.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Dative of deadline. 1. 'К' governs the dative. 2. 'Времени' is the dative with the -ен- oblique stem. 3. 'Этому' agrees as a dative neuter pronoun: by this time everyone had left.
Strategic focus: Instrumental with за. 1. 'За' here takes the instrumental. 2. 'Временем' shows the -ен- oblique stem plus instrumental ending -ем. 3. The sentence means try to keep track of time.
Strategic focus: Instrumental idiom. 1. 'Со' takes the instrumental. 2. 'Временем' uses the heteroclitic -ен- oblique stem. 3. A common idiom meaning over time everything gradually changes.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 1. 'О' governs the prepositional. 2. 'Времени' is the prepositional with the -ен- oblique stem. 3. The sentence means we agreed on the time of the meeting.
Strategic focus: Prepositional idiom. 1. 'Во время' is a fixed phrase taking a genitive complement. 2. Here 'урока' is genitive. 3. The whole unit means don't talk during the lesson.

missions.phrase: Я взял эту книгу на время.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative idiom. 1. 'На' here takes the accusative. 2. 'Время' is accusative, identical to the nominative for this neuter noun. 3. 'На время' means for a while, temporarily.

missions.phrase: В выходные у меня есть свободное время.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Adjective agreement. 1. 'Свободное' agrees with 'время' as neuter nominative. 2. The noun stays in its base form (no -ен- stem). 3. The sentence means on weekends I have free time.

missions.phrase: В наше время все пользуются интернетом.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Adjective agreement idiom. 1. 'Наше' agrees with 'время' as neuter. 2. 'В' takes the accusative in this fixed phrase. 3. 'В наше время' means nowadays, in our day.
Strategic focus: Genitive object. 1. 'Много' governs the genitive. 2. 'Времени' carries the heteroclitic -ен- oblique stem. 3. The sentence means I'm afraid of wasting a lot of time.

missions.phrase: Я всё время работаю без отдыха.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative adverbial. 1. 'Всё время' is an accusative time-phrase acting as an adverb. 2. The noun keeps its base neuter form. 3. The sentence means I work all the time without rest.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 1. 'Времена́' is the irregular plural with end stress. 2. 'Тяжёлые' agrees as plural. 3. 'Прошли' agrees in the plural: these hard times have finally passed.

missions.phrase: Этот обычай известен с давних времён.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 1. 'С' here governs the genitive. 2. 'Времён' is the genitive plural with ё. 3. 'Давних' agrees as plural: this custom is known since ancient times.

missions.phrase: Нам пора найти время для отдыха.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative object. 1. 'Найти' takes a direct object. 2. 'Время' is accusative, matching the nominative for this neuter noun. 3. The sentence means it's time to find time to rest.
Strategic focus: Dative deadline. 1. 'К' governs the dative. 2. 'Времени' uses the heteroclitic -ен- oblique stem in the dative. 3. The sentence means be ready by this time.
